title: Japan's 'Snow Monkey Park' to Limit Visitor Numbers
paragraphs: The snow monkeys of Nagano are very famous. Every winter, many tourists come to see the wild monkeys sitting in a hot spring in the snow. But now, the park has started a new system to control the number of visitors.
The park is called Jigokudani Yaen-koen, or Jigokudani Monkey Park. It is in the mountains of Nagano Prefecture. The monkeys there are Japanese macaques, and they are wild animals.
In August 2026, the park started selling tickets online. Visitors choose a date and a time to visit. After they pay, they get a ticket with a QR code. Tickets go on sale 90 days before the visit.

The park is the most crowded from December to March, when there is snow. It is also very busy during Japanese holidays, such as Golden Week. During these busy times, visitors must buy tickets in advance. People who arrive without a ticket may have to wait a long time, or they may not be able to enter.

Why did the park make this change? Recently, about 3,000 to 4,000 people have visited the park every day. There were very long lines at the ticket office. Some visitors also tried to touch or feed the monkeys, or even to get into the hot spring with them. According to the Japan Times, the park plans to allow only about 2,000 visitors a day.
Visitors should remember that the monkeys are wild. Sometimes they may not come to the hot spring, and tickets cannot be returned for money if there are no monkeys.
